text:
maya: Hey @support, customer reports 401 invalid_api_key after a recent secret-manager migration. They say calls used to succeed, now get "invalid_api_key".

jordan: Which secret manager? GCP secret manager or our internal sync?

maya: GCP. They migrated secrets from project `redwood-staging` -> `redwood-prod-locked` and updated the secret URI in k8s. Pod logs show fetch succeeded, but API returns 401.

samir: Can you paste the full Authorization header (redacted) and the secret resource name they used? sometimes path vs version mismatch happens.

maya: Header (redacted): `Authorization: Bearer xxxxx...` (length looks shorter than other valid keys). Secret path they set: `projects/redwood-prod-locked/secrets/redwood-api-key` (no `versions/1`).
jordan: Ah — if they point at the secret without `/versions/<n>` some client libraries return the latest but others return a metadata object. Did their sync agent fetch the secret value or the secret resource metadata?

maya: I grabbed pod env: `REDWOOD_KEY_URI=sm://projects/redwood-prod-locked/secrets/redwood-api-key` and our fetcher logs: `GET /v1/projects/redwood-prod-locked/secrets/redwood-api-key: OK` then `value: "{"name":"projects/...","replication":{...}}"` — looks like JSON metadata, not the secret string.

samir: That explains it. They stored the JSON object (secret resource) as the API key string. Key would be malformed -> shorter and invalid -> 401.

support-engineer: Short repro steps: 1) Exec into pod 2) `echo $REDWOOD_APIKEY` 3) check length: should be ~40-60 chars. If you see `{` or `name:` it's the resource object.

jordan: Quick fix: update the fetcher to call `access` endpoint or use the client library accessor that returns `payload.data` (GCP). Example curl:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GCP_TOKEN" "https://secretmanager.googleapis.com/v1/projects/redwood-prod-locked/secrets/redwood-api-key/versions/latest:access" | jq -r '.payload.data' | base64 --decode
```

maya: I forwarded that to the customer. They tried the curl and got back a long base64 string -> decoded to a 52-char token. Replaced env var with that value and calls succeeded.

samir: Two follow-ups: 1) Recommend adding a validation check in bootstrap: ensure API key matches regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,64}$` and fail fast. 2) Add a migration playbook note: if secret manager response contains `replication`/`name`, you pulled metadata.

support-engineer: Filing internal KB: `support/secret-manager-metadata-misfetch.md` with steps and sample commands. Also suggest a proactive scan for clusters with `REDWOOD_KEY_URI` still pointing to old pattern.

infra-bot: Automated note: Created KB ticket #SUP-4512 and scheduled a scanner job to run in 24h across GCP projects.

maya: Customer confirmed no further 401s after replacement. Closing on their side but keeping KB open. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Nice catch. Adding an optional alert: if auth fails >=5 times in 10m after a secret rotation, surface a hint "check secret payload vs metadata" in the support UI.

maya: Will do. Thanks everyone. :pray:
